Transformation · Iteration · Evolution · Est. 2022 · Philadelphia
01 — Company
Who we are
The company
AI-powered personal development tools running on infrastructure we control. Philadelphia. Founded 2022. Your health data never leaves our hardware. That's not marketing — it's architecture.
The product
The Spark — wellness coaching intake and habit-tracking app. You open it when you want to log something. Friday it asks how your week went. It shows you what you actually did versus what you said you'd do.
The summer campaign
100 Days of Summer — a Drexel IRB-reviewed field study. Track habits for 100 days. Wawa gift card lottery at the end. "wawawednesday.com" is the public URL. Fan energy, not Wawa partnership.
The brand truth
We are a precision instrument. Not a motivational poster. Not a fitness app. Not a meditation app. Not a journal app with AI bolted on. "No judgment. Just what happened." — that's the whole thing.
02 — Identity
The logo system
Every WCN product has a punctuation mark as its logo. The company is a question — What Comes Next? — and each product is a different kind of answer. Every mark lives in a circular badge with ring text: WHAT COMES NEXT LLC — TRANSFORMATION ITERATION EVOLUTION — 2022. The ghost ? lives inside every product mark. The question never goes away. The answer just gets louder.
The company mark — ?
Off-white on teal #216869
The origin. The only mark on teal. Use for company-wide comms, pitch materials, homepage. Never on product-specific materials alone.
The Spark — !
Coral #e76f51 on black
Action. The moment a question becomes a decision. The ghost ? shares the dot at the base. Warm, immediate, energetic without aggressive.
The Catalyst — %
Amber #f4a261 on near-black
Balance under rotation. Infrastructure color. Two circles held in tension by a diagonal bar. Not consumer-facing — appears in technical and investor contexts.
The !? compound mark — ambassador + campaign
Coral fill + off-white ghost · Dark field version shown
The question and the answer existing simultaneously, physically overlapping. This is what the world sees first on visors and the mobile splash screen. Designed to work small — hats, stickers, loading screens. On white merch: coral fill + coral outline (same color, two weights).
Coach face
Gold #F5C518 on black
Warm, authoritative
Admin face
Black on gold #EAAA00
Data-forward, precise
Badge rule: Dark backgrounds only for the standard badge system. The marks were designed for dark surfaces — layering effects, ghost marks, colored rings all depend on dark contrast. The Admin Face inversion is deliberate, not an exception.
03 — Color
The palette
#216869
Primary brand teal
The company. Calm, trustworthy. Company mark background only — never used as product accent.
#e76f51
Warm coral
The Spark. Action, warmth, ignition. CTAs, the ! mark, "Save Entry" button.
#f4a261
Amber
The Catalyst (inference engine). Infrastructure color — not in consumer-facing design.
#f4f4f4
Off-white
Light surface + the company ? mark color. Not white. The distinction matters at print scale.
#2d3436
Charcoal
Body text on light surfaces. Never pure black — charcoal reads softer and more intentional.
#EAAA00
Warm goldCoach's Clipboard UI
#F5C518
Referee goldBadge system only
#49a078
SageData viz only
#0a0a0a
Product blackBadge backgrounds
#110e09
Warm near-blackCatalyst badge bg
The warm progression: Coral → Amber → Gold. Each is a distinct product color. Together they read as a family — warmer and brighter as you move from user-facing (Spark/coral) through infrastructure (Catalyst/amber) to professional admin (Clipboard/gold). Preserve this in any new product work.

What not to do: Don't put coral and amber together without a strong neutral separator — they're both warm and will fight. Don't put standard badges on light backgrounds. Don't use Referee Gold #F5C518 in body text or small UI elements — badge color only.
04 — Type
Typography
Display Bold 700 · 48px+ What Comes Next? Taglines, covers, hero headings
Heading SemiBold 600 · 24–36px 100 Days of Summer Section titles, screen headers
Subheading Medium 500 · 18–22px Sword Sharpening Session Card titles, navigation, labels
Body Regular 400 · 14–16px No judgment. Just what happened. Paragraph text, descriptions
Badge ring Light 300 · 8–11px tracked TRANSFORMATION · ITERATION · EVOLUTION Badge circumference only
Primary font: Raleway — Google Fonts, free, open license. Geometric sans-serif with distinctive letterforms (especially the uppercase W and lowercase e). Modern without being cold. The only typeface. No serifs — ever.

Code contexts: JetBrains Mono or Fira Code — both free, both compatible with the overall aesthetic.
05 — Voice
How we sound
We do
Direct. Specific. Zero filler
Name specific things — the habit, the day, the number
Use the participant's own language back to them
Let silence and whitespace do work
Warmth through specificity, not exclamation points
Acknowledge when something is hard without suggesting it shouldn't be
We don't
Journey. Empower. Holistic. Unlock. Seamless.
Moralize about user choices
Sanitize user language back to them
Generic closers that could be for anyone
Passive voice to avoid accountability
Describe ourselves as "smart" or "AI-powered" without specifics
The one-sentence ambassador pitch for the app
"You open it when you want to log something. Could be 30 seconds. Could be longer. Friday it asks how your week went. You write whatever you want. It shows you what you actually did versus what you said you'd do. No judgment. Just what happened."
06 — Campaign
Summer 2026 merch context
What's ordered / in production
White Flexfit visor — coral !? mark (Printful)
Magnetic notepads 2×3.5" — teal bg, !? mark, habit checkboxes, QR code linking to wawawednesday.com (Canva Print)
Lanyard + badge — "AMBASSADOR / 100 Days of Summer" printed card
The hero shot to capture
Ambassador and prospective participant leaning over a notebook. A real conversation caught naturally. The notebook is not the hero. The moment is. Content creator's job is to be ready when it happens.
!? on light surfaces (visors, white merch, print on white): The ! is coral fill (#e76f51). The ? is a coral outline — same color, two weights, one mark. On dark surfaces: ! is coral fill, ? is off-white outline.
The Wawa principle: Fan energy, not partner energy. Say "Wawa" freely. Use photos of purchased Wawa products. Never use the Wawa logo, font, or brand assets. "There will be Wawa" does the same job as the logo — and it's actually more on-brand.
